goal: A large working vocabulary in Northern (Hà Nội) Vietnamese first, then short sentence patterns, then conversation.

phases.title: Core vocabulary
phases.target: About 300 words the learner can recognise by ear and recall by meaning (meaning strength 0.8 or more).
phases.exit: Move on when about 250 words are in the review deck or on the known list and recent meaning strength averages 0.8 or more.

phases.title: Short sentence patterns
phases.target: Twenty high-value patterns built from known words: Tôi muốn ..., ... ở đâu?, Cái này bao nhiêu tiền?, Có ... không?, Tôi là ..., Tôi không ..., ... được không?
phases.exit: The learner builds and understands each pattern with known words at 0.8 or more.

phases.title: Conversation battles
phases.target: The foe speaks lines of a short dialogue and the learner picks or types replies: ordering food, a taxi, the market, meeting people.

units.title: Food and drink
units.notes: The learner already knew almost all of it; only gà, cá and bò needed practice. The other nine are on the known list.

units.title: Big numbers and prices
units.notes: Numbers 0 to 10 are a warm-up only. Brings in the nặng and ngã tones (triệu, chục, nữa, rưỡi) that lesson 1 lacked, and the hỏi and ngã contrast (nửa and nữa, rẻ and rẽ).

units.title: People and family
units.foeIdea: Cô Hàng Xóm, the nosy neighbour who asks about everyone in your family.
units.notes: Explain that family words double as I and you. Hà Nội says bố and mẹ (the South says ba and má).

units.title: Greetings and politeness
units.foeIdea: Ông Khó Tính, the grumpy old man who only softens when you are polite.
units.notes: ạ at the end of a sentence to older people; vâng is the typical Northern polite yes.

units.title: Everyday verbs
units.foeIdea: Thần Lười, the spirit of laziness who wants you to stay on the sofa.
units.notes: Likely partly known: use a warm-up for ăn, uống, đi, có, là. Verbs unlock the patterns phase.

units.title: Describing words
units.foeIdea: Gương Thần, a vain magic mirror that describes everything wrongly.
units.notes: rét is the Northern word for cold weather (lạnh also works). Describing words follow the noun.

units.title: Places in the city
units.foeIdea: Xe Máy Điên, the runaway scooter that weaves through the Old Quarter.
units.notes: phố and ga were contrast words in lesson 1; reuse that memory.

units.title: Time and days
units.foeIdea: Đồng Hồ Ngủ Gật, the dozing clock that makes you late.
units.notes: muộn is Northern for late (the South says trễ). năm (year) was a warm-up gloss in lesson 2.

units.title: Question words
units.foeIdea: Con Vẹt Hỏi, the parrot that only ever asks questions.
units.notes: thế nào is Northern (the South prefers sao or như thế nào). Bridges into the patterns phase.

units.title: Getting around
units.foeIdea: Ông Tắc Đường, Mr Traffic Jam. Note that Hà Nội says tắc đường; the South says kẹt xe.
units.notes: rẽ was a contrast word in lesson 2 (rẻ against rẽ).

units.title: At the market
units.foeIdea: Chuột Chợ, the market rat that steals from every stall.
units.notes: quả and thịt lợn are Northern (the South says trái and thịt heo). Builds on lesson 2 prices.

units.title: Colours and clothes
units.foeIdea: a chameleon that keeps changing colour.
units.notes: xanh covers blue and green; mũ is Northern for hat (the South says nón).

units.title: The body and feeling unwell
units.notes: ốm is Northern for ill (the South says bệnh).

units.title: Weather and seasons in Hà Nội
units.foeIdea: Bà Mưa Phùn, Lady Drizzle, who brings Hà Nội's damp spring.
units.notes: mây was a contrast word in lesson 2. nồm is the damp, sticky Hà Nội spring weather.
